The present opposite parties and their predecessors-in-interest as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 24 of 1958 which was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 157 of 1.963 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Noakhali for partition. Subsequently out of a compromise some of the parties were transposed and the opposite party No. 1 and 2 of the instant revisional application were made defendant Nos. 12 and 12(ka) of the said suit. The trial Court decreed the suit on preliminary form on 30-1-1966, against which the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 170 of 1966 before the District Judge, Feni the then Noakhali wherein the present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 were made respondent Nos. 21 and 22 and the appeal was allowed and the suit was decreed on compromise. Thereafter pursuant to the preliminary decree the final decree was drawn on 20-8-1990 by the Subordinate Judge, Additional Court, Noakhali. Thereafter the present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 i.e. the decree-holder defendant Nos.12 and 12(ka) and 2 others filed Execution Case being No.2 of 1992 for taking possession in the suit land on the basis of the aforesaid final decree. During pendency of the Execution Case the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 of the present revisional application sold certain properties from the suit property to the present petitioner in the years 1996, 1997 and 1998 by registered sale deeds as well as hand over the possession thereon. All on a sudden on 9-6-2006 the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 who filed, the aforesaid Execution Case filed an application in the said case for striking out the lands mentioned in the schedule of the application from the execution proceeding. In the application it has been stated that the opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 of the present revisional application filed Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 impleading the defendant Nos.12 and 12(ka) i.e. the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as defendants. Thereafter the parties executed a solenama and the suit was dismissed on compromise and, as such, the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 have no claim in the lands mentioned in the application for exclusion. The executing Court vide order dated 20-2-2006 allowed the same. 

 14. But it appears that admittedly the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 who are defendants in the aforesaid suit as well as applicants of the Execution Case transferred the property in question in favour of the petitioner in the years 1996, 1997 and 1998 by registered sale deeds as well as hand over possession. Subsequently, it appears that the added opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 who were wrongly added as opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 in present revisional application filed Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 impleading the present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as defendants, wherein the plaintiffs prayed for a declaration that the judgment and decree passed in the present title suit for partition is not binding upon the plaintiffs. The present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as defendants entered appearance and filed a compromise petition resulting dismissal of the suit. On perusal of the said solenama as well as the judgment and decree passed by that suit it appears that though the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 transferred the land in favour of the petitioners long before filing of the said suit i.e. Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 but the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 neither disclosed anything the transfer nor mentioned the names of the petitioners in any manner. It appears that in the line of the compromise decree obtained in Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are now trying to strike out certain lands from the executing process. On the facts and circumstances, it appears that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 suppressed relevant fact in the Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 which not only suppression of fact but also practicing fraud upon the Court of law.
